observations: Photo 0 shows the internal components of a laptop with the motherboard exposed, including the CPU fan, RAM slots, and various connectors. The chassis appears to be black with visible wear.
Photo 1 is a similar view of the internal components, with a sticker visible near the bottom right that reads 'Dell P51027' and 'Made in China'.
Photo 2 shows the exterior of the laptop with the screen open, displaying the Dell logo on the bezel and a full keyboard. The laptop is dark gray or black, and the screen is off.
The seller claims it is a 'Dell 3420' with an '11th gen Core i5' processor, but no such model exists for Dell 3420 — the 3420 is a 14-inch model from 2014, which uses 4th gen Intel processors.
The sticker in photo 1 (Dell P51027) is a part number, not a model number. It may be a service tag or component ID, not indicative of the laptop model.
No visible model number or label on the chassis or screen bezel in any photo.
The photos show a modern-looking laptop with a slim design, which is inconsistent with the Dell 3420, which had a bulkier design and different keyboard layout.
The seller's claim of '11th gen Core i5' is unverifiable from the photos — no CPU is visible, and the motherboard does not show a socket or branding that confirms the generation.
